title: sampled-span-deduplication-and-id-canonicalizer
creator: Marina Chen
description:
Problem: We see duplicated spans in our tracing pipeline for a subset of high-throughput frontends and edge proxies where retries, speculative fanout, or SDK buffering cause the same logical span to be emitted multiple times. Duplicates inflate storage costs, pollute error/latency dashboards, and complicate span-based analysis (root cause, allocation by route).

Goal: Implement a combined SDK + ingest-side strategy that (1) generates a stable, canonical span identifier for logically-equivalent spans across SDKs and proxies, (2) deduplicates sampled spans at ingest with a short-time window to avoid double-counting without materially increasing end-to-end trace latency, and (3) keeps the feature toggleable per-customer/route.

Approach summary:
- SDK & Middleware changes: introduce a CanonicalSpanID hook in language SDKs and middleware adapters that computes a stable fingerprint for a span at close/export time. Fingerprint inputs: normalized trace_id, normalized parent_id or pseudo-parent (if missing), span_name (normalized), start_time bucket (millisecond precision), and a protobuf-style semantic hashing of resource attributes that are included in sampling decisions. The hook attaches header "X-Redwood-Canonical-Span" to exported spans over OTLP/HTTP/gRPC exporters.
- Edge/Proxy normalization: edge proxy adapters will normalize incoming span headers (strip noise from client-generated ids, map legacy headers to canonical header) and propagate "X-Redwood-Canonical-Span" downstream when available.
- Ingest dedup window: server-side ingest will keep a small in-memory bloom/TTL map for canonical ids per tenant for a configurable window (default 200ms). If a canonical id repeats within the window, we drop the duplicate and emit a dedup metric. For unsampled spans (sampled=false) we do not store; deduplication only applies to sampled spans to avoid state explosion.
- Sampling alignment: when SAMPLING_HINT headers are present, the canonicalizer includes hint version to avoid collapsing spans with different sampling decisions.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Short window (200ms) chosen to collapse immediate duplicates from retries/fanout while keeping ingest path low-latency. Longer windows reduce duplicates more but require more memory and increase edge-case chance of dropping legitimately distinct spans.
- We keep dedupserver memory bounded by tenant by aging entries and using a compact hash set (probabilistic bloom for higher-scale tenants) to avoid OOM. Exact-on behavior is supported for top-tier customers behind a feature flag.
- Canonical ID must be deterministic and stable across SDK versions; we version the hashing scheme (v1) and include scheme version in header to allow future migration.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement CanonicalSpanID v1 in node and python SDKs behind opt-in flag (sdk.config.enableCanonicalSpanV1). Add middleware adapter for express/fastify and python ASGI/Werkzeug that sets header when exporting.
2) Deploy ingest-side deduper to canary region for internal traffic with dedup metrics enabled. Measure dedup rate, ingestion CPU/latency impact, and false-positives (reported as dropped_trace_rate).
3) Extend to edge proxy adapters (envoy filter) and enable for a small set of customers.
4) Bump SDK stable minor release, create migration guide, and flip opt-in to default for new customers after two weeks of telemetry showing low FP

Data and tests:
- Benchmarks: microbench SDK overhead (allocations per span), ingestion latency P50/P95 before and after dedup store on canary, memory overhead per tenant. Goal: SDK overhead < 0.5% CPU, ingest P95 latency increase < 3ms at 99th percentile.
- Integration tests: replaying previously captured duplicated traces to verify dedup works and preserving trace graph connectivity.
- Metrics: tracing.dedup.count, tracing.dedup.rate, tracing.dedup.false_positive, tracing.canonical_id_generation_errors, tracing.ingest.dedup_latency_p95.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- Create a new Observability Console card showing dedup rate over time by customer and route and how dedup impacts tokenized span counts. Add an alert if dedup_rate > 5% for a stable production route (indicates potential SDK misbehavior).

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Should canonicalization include certain resource attributes (service.version, env) by default? Added to TODO for product decision.
- For streaming export (continuous spans mid-flight), when should canonical ID be computed? We choose compute-at-export to capture final sanitized attributes.

2026-03-01 - Engineering note: prototype in node-sdk completed; canonical id computation adds ~120ns median per span in microbenchmarks. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1287

2026-03-07 - Security review: scoped to instrumentation headers; no sensitive data added. Auth team OK with header naming. Security review flagged legacy header collisions; added normalization step.
